Description.en: To be used as default value if no value is provided or when no special coded qualification is assumed. Usually, it can be assumed that the source agency assigns sufficient confidence to the provided observation and/or the value is not expected to be dramatically revised.

Observations are characterised as such when different content exists or a different methodology has been applied to this observation as compared with the preceding one (the one given for the previous period).
Used to indicate slight deviations from the established methodology (footnote-type information); these divergences do not imply a break in time series.

Observation obtained through an estimation methodology (e.g. to produce back-casts) or based on the use of a limited amount of data or ad hoc sampling and through additional calculations (e.g. to produce a value at an early stage of the production stage while not all data are available). It may also be used in case of experimental data (e.g. in the context of a pilot ahead of a full scale production process) or in case of data of (anticipated/assessed) low quality. If needed, additional information can be provided through free text using the COMMENT_OBS attribute at the observation level or at a higher level. This code is to be used when the estimation is done by a sender agency. When the imputation is carried out by a receiver agency in order to replace or fill gaps in reported data series, the flag to use is I "Value imputed by a receiving agency".

Value deemed to assess the magnitude which a quantity will assume at some future point of time (as distinct from "estimated value" which attempts to assess the magnitude of an already existent quantity).
Data collected on the basis of definitions or (alternative) collection methods under development. Data not of guaranteed quality as normally expected from provider.

This code is used when data for a given category are missing and are included in another category, sub-total or total. Generally where code "K" is used there should be a corresponding code "W - Includes data from another category" assigned to the over-covered category. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify under which category the data are included.

This code is used when data include another category, or go beyond the scope of the data collection and are therefore over-covered. Generally, where code "W" is used there should be a corresponding code "K - Data included in another category" assigned to the category which is under-covered. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify which additional data are included.

This code is to be used when no breakdown is made between the reasons why data are missing. Data can be missing due to many reasons: data cannot exist, data exist but are not collected (e.g. because they are below a certain threshold or subject to a derogation clause), data are unreliable, etc.

Used to denote empty cells resulting from the impossibility to collect a statistical value (e.g. a particular education level or type of institution may be not applicable to a given country's education system).

An observation is characterised as "provisional" when the source agency - while it bases its calculations on its standard production methodology - considers that the data, almost certainly, are expected to be revised.
Special circumstances (e.g. strike) affecting the observation or causing a missing value.

Name.en: Missing value; data exist but were not collected

Description.en: Used, for example, when some data are not reported/disseminated because they are below a certain threshold.
Used in some daily data flows.
Used, for example, when data are suppressed due to statistical confidentiality considerations.

Clause in an agreement (e.g. legal act, gentlemen's agreement) stating that some provisions in the agreement are not to be implemented by designated parties; these derogations may affect the observation or cause a missing value. In general, derogations are limited in time.
Used to indicate a value which is not a "real" zero (e.g. a result of 0.0004 rounded to zero).
This indicates existing observations, but for which the user should also be aware of the low quality assigned.
Observation as received from the respondent without further evaluation of data quality.
A value that is calculated or estimated, rather than directly observed or measured.

A value that is estimated or assigned when it cannot be directly measured or observed. Observation imputed by a receiving agency to replace or fill gaps in reported data series. This code is intended to cover all cases where a receiving agency publishes data about a sending agency that do not come from an official source in the sender agency's reporting framework. When the estimation is done by the sender agency, the flag to use is E "Estimated value".
Data that is estimated or calculated based on information obtained from counterpart countries.
This code is used when the observation status (rather than the value) is not available.

Name.en: Observation status unavailable from external organisation

Description.en: This code is used when the observation is from an external organization and the observation status (rather than the value) is not available. The observation may be from an external organization that does not use any system of flags when sharing data. Implementers should use attributes at the observation-level or at a higher-level such as: COMMENT_OBS, DATA_SOURCE or NATURE, to provide information on the source or nature.

This code is used when data exclude one or several subcategories that it should normally include, resulting in under-coverage of the category. This situation typically arises when the category is an aggregate and code ‘K’ or ‘O’ applies to one (or several) of its subcategories.

Name.en: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods

Description.en: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods.

Name.en: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods

Description.en: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods.
Non-transformed data (also called original data) refers to data in its original form, before any mathematical or statistical operations have been applied to change its values or distribution.

Data that results from direct calculations or transformations performed on raw data by IMF staff. These calculations are usually straightforward and transparent, with the published numbers easily traceable back to the source data.

Name.en: IMF Staff calculations (derived from counterpart data)

Description.en: Data resulting from direct application of counterpart data by IMF staff to the official information reported by other countries.

Data derived through calculations or transformations on available source data, where some necessary information might be missing. In these cases, IMF staff uses estimates to fill in the gaps and produce the published numbers.

Forecasts of future values for a time series, constructed using various techniques such as statistical modeling, trend analysis, and expert judgment. These projections are based on historical data, current economic conditions, and other relevant factors.
Data that combines both raw and derived data. This could occur when some components of a dataset are directly reported while others are calculated or estimated.
Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities without any modifications or adjustments made by IMF staff.

Name.en: Reported official data converted to US dollar

Description.en: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities in a country's domestic currency, which IMF staff then converts to US dollars using appropriate exchange rates.
Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities that has that have been adjusted using internal IMF records.
Third party data.

Description.en: To be used as default value if no value is provided or when no special coded qualification is assumed. Usually, it can be assumed that the source agency assigns sufficient confidence to the provided observation and/or the value is not expected to be dramatically revised.

Observations are characterised as such when different content exists or a different methodology has been applied to this observation as compared with the preceding one (the one given for the previous period).
Used to indicate slight deviations from the established methodology (footnote-type information); these divergences do not imply a break in time series.

Observation obtained through an estimation methodology (e.g. to produce back-casts) or based on the use of a limited amount of data or ad hoc sampling and through additional calculations (e.g. to produce a value at an early stage of the production stage while not all data are available). It may also be used in case of experimental data (e.g. in the context of a pilot ahead of a full scale production process) or in case of data of (anticipated/assessed) low quality. If needed, additional information can be provided through free text using the COMMENT_OBS attribute at the observation level or at a higher level. This code is to be used when the estimation is done by a sender agency. When the imputation is carried out by a receiver agency in order to replace or fill gaps in reported data series, the flag to use is I "Value imputed by a receiving agency".

Value deemed to assess the magnitude which a quantity will assume at some future point of time (as distinct from "estimated value" which attempts to assess the magnitude of an already existent quantity).
Data collected on the basis of definitions or (alternative) collection methods under development. Data not of guaranteed quality as normally expected from provider.

This code is used when data for a given category are missing and are included in another category, sub-total or total. Generally where code "K" is used there should be a corresponding code "W - Includes data from another category" assigned to the over-covered category. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify under which category the data are included.

This code is used when data include another category, or go beyond the scope of the data collection and are therefore over-covered. Generally, where code "W" is used there should be a corresponding code "K - Data included in another category" assigned to the category which is under-covered. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify which additional data are included.

This code is to be used when no breakdown is made between the reasons why data are missing. Data can be missing due to many reasons: data cannot exist, data exist but are not collected (e.g. because they are below a certain threshold or subject to a derogation clause), data are unreliable, etc.

Used to denote empty cells resulting from the impossibility to collect a statistical value (e.g. a particular education level or type of institution may be not applicable to a given country's education system).

An observation is characterised as "provisional" when the source agency - while it bases its calculations on its standard production methodology - considers that the data, almost certainly, are expected to be revised.
Special circumstances (e.g. strike) affecting the observation or causing a missing value.

Name.en: Missing value; data exist but were not collected

Description.en: Used, for example, when some data are not reported/disseminated because they are below a certain threshold.
Used in some daily data flows.
Used, for example, when data are suppressed due to statistical confidentiality considerations.

Clause in an agreement (e.g. legal act, gentlemen's agreement) stating that some provisions in the agreement are not to be implemented by designated parties; these derogations may affect the observation or cause a missing value. In general, derogations are limited in time.
Used to indicate a value which is not a "real" zero (e.g. a result of 0.0004 rounded to zero).
This indicates existing observations, but for which the user should also be aware of the low quality assigned.
Observation as received from the respondent without further evaluation of data quality.
A value that is calculated or estimated, rather than directly observed or measured.

A value that is estimated or assigned when it cannot be directly measured or observed. Observation imputed by a receiving agency to replace or fill gaps in reported data series. This code is intended to cover all cases where a receiving agency publishes data about a sending agency that do not come from an official source in the sender agency's reporting framework. When the estimation is done by the sender agency, the flag to use is E "Estimated value".
Data that is estimated or calculated based on information obtained from counterpart countries.
This code is used when the observation status (rather than the value) is not available.

Name.en: Observation status unavailable from external organisation

Description.en: This code is used when the observation is from an external organization and the observation status (rather than the value) is not available. The observation may be from an external organization that does not use any system of flags when sharing data. Implementers should use attributes at the observation-level or at a higher-level such as: COMMENT_OBS, DATA_SOURCE or NATURE, to provide information on the source or nature.

This code is used when data exclude one or several subcategories that it should normally include, resulting in under-coverage of the category. This situation typically arises when the category is an aggregate and code ‘K’ or ‘O’ applies to one (or several) of its subcategories.

Name.en: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods

Description.en: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods.

Name.en: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods

Description.en: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods.
Non-transformed data (also called original data) refers to data in its original form, before any mathematical or statistical operations have been applied to change its values or distribution.

Data that results from direct calculations or transformations performed on raw data by IMF staff. These calculations are usually straightforward and transparent, with the published numbers easily traceable back to the source data.

Name.en: IMF Staff calculations (derived from counterpart data)

Description.en: Data resulting from direct application of counterpart data by IMF staff to the official information reported by other countries.

Data derived through calculations or transformations on available source data, where some necessary information might be missing. In these cases, IMF staff uses estimates to fill in the gaps and produce the published numbers.

Forecasts of future values for a time series, constructed using various techniques such as statistical modeling, trend analysis, and expert judgment. These projections are based on historical data, current economic conditions, and other relevant factors.
Data that combines both raw and derived data. This could occur when some components of a dataset are directly reported while others are calculated or estimated.
Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities without any modifications or adjustments made by IMF staff.

Name.en: Reported official data converted to US dollar

Description.en: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities in a country's domestic currency, which IMF staff then converts to US dollars using appropriate exchange rates.
Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities that has that have been adjusted using internal IMF records.
Third party data.

Description.en: To be used as default value if no value is provided or when no special coded qualification is assumed. Usually, it can be assumed that the source agency assigns sufficient confidence to the provided observation and/or the value is not expected to be dramatically revised.

Observations are characterised as such when different content exists or a different methodology has been applied to this observation as compared with the preceding one (the one given for the previous period).
Used to indicate slight deviations from the established methodology (footnote-type information); these divergences do not imply a break in time series.

Observation obtained through an estimation methodology (e.g. to produce back-casts) or based on the use of a limited amount of data or ad hoc sampling and through additional calculations (e.g. to produce a value at an early stage of the production stage while not all data are available). It may also be used in case of experimental data (e.g. in the context of a pilot ahead of a full scale production process) or in case of data of (anticipated/assessed) low quality. If needed, additional information can be provided through free text using the COMMENT_OBS attribute at the observation level or at a higher level. This code is to be used when the estimation is done by a sender agency. When the imputation is carried out by a receiver agency in order to replace or fill gaps in reported data series, the flag to use is I "Value imputed by a receiving agency".

Value deemed to assess the magnitude which a quantity will assume at some future point of time (as distinct from "estimated value" which attempts to assess the magnitude of an already existent quantity).
Data collected on the basis of definitions or (alternative) collection methods under development. Data not of guaranteed quality as normally expected from provider.

This code is used when data for a given category are missing and are included in another category, sub-total or total. Generally where code "K" is used there should be a corresponding code "W - Includes data from another category" assigned to the over-covered category. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify under which category the data are included.

This code is used when data include another category, or go beyond the scope of the data collection and are therefore over-covered. Generally, where code "W" is used there should be a corresponding code "K - Data included in another category" assigned to the category which is under-covered. Implementers and data reporters should use the COMMENT_OBS observation-level attribute to specify which additional data are included.

This code is to be used when no breakdown is made between the reasons why data are missing. Data can be missing due to many reasons: data cannot exist, data exist but are not collected (e.g. because they are below a certain threshold or subject to a derogation clause), data are unreliable, etc.

Used to denote empty cells resulting from the impossibility to collect a statistical value (e.g. a particular education level or type of institution may be not applicable to a given country's education system).

An observation is characterised as "provisional" when the source agency - while it bases its calculations on its standard production methodology - considers that the data, almost certainly, are expected to be revised.
Special circumstances (e.g. strike) affecting the observation or causing a missing value.

Name.en: Missing value; data exist but were not collected

Description.en: Used, for example, when some data are not reported/disseminated because they are below a certain threshold.
Used in some daily data flows.
Used, for example, when data are suppressed due to statistical confidentiality considerations.

Clause in an agreement (e.g. legal act, gentlemen's agreement) stating that some provisions in the agreement are not to be implemented by designated parties; these derogations may affect the observation or cause a missing value. In general, derogations are limited in time.
Used to indicate a value which is not a "real" zero (e.g. a result of 0.0004 rounded to zero).
This indicates existing observations, but for which the user should also be aware of the low quality assigned.
Observation as received from the respondent without further evaluation of data quality.
A value that is calculated or estimated, rather than directly observed or measured.

A value that is estimated or assigned when it cannot be directly measured or observed. Observation imputed by a receiving agency to replace or fill gaps in reported data series. This code is intended to cover all cases where a receiving agency publishes data about a sending agency that do not come from an official source in the sender agency's reporting framework. When the estimation is done by the sender agency, the flag to use is E "Estimated value".
Data that is estimated or calculated based on information obtained from counterpart countries.
This code is used when the observation status (rather than the value) is not available.

Name.en: Observation status unavailable from external organisation

Description.en: This code is used when the observation is from an external organization and the observation status (rather than the value) is not available. The observation may be from an external organization that does not use any system of flags when sharing data. Implementers should use attributes at the observation-level or at a higher-level such as: COMMENT_OBS, DATA_SOURCE or NATURE, to provide information on the source or nature.

This code is used when data exclude one or several subcategories that it should normally include, resulting in under-coverage of the category. This situation typically arises when the category is an aggregate and code ‘K’ or ‘O’ applies to one (or several) of its subcategories.

Name.en: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods

Description.en: Staff estimates using group mean imputation methods.

Name.en: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods

Description.en: Staff estimates using historical imputation methods.
Non-transformed data (also called original data) refers to data in its original form, before any mathematical or statistical operations have been applied to change its values or distribution.

Data that results from direct calculations or transformations performed on raw data by IMF staff. These calculations are usually straightforward and transparent, with the published numbers easily traceable back to the source data.

Name.en: IMF Staff calculations (derived from counterpart data)

Description.en: Data resulting from direct application of counterpart data by IMF staff to the official information reported by other countries.

Data derived through calculations or transformations on available source data, where some necessary information might be missing. In these cases, IMF staff uses estimates to fill in the gaps and produce the published numbers.

Forecasts of future values for a time series, constructed using various techniques such as statistical modeling, trend analysis, and expert judgment. These projections are based on historical data, current economic conditions, and other relevant factors.
Data that combines both raw and derived data. This could occur when some components of a dataset are directly reported while others are calculated or estimated.
Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities without any modifications or adjustments made by IMF staff.

Name.en: Reported official data converted to US dollar

Description.en: Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities in a country's domestic currency, which IMF staff then converts to US dollars using appropriate exchange rates.
Official data reported to the IMF by country authorities that has that have been adjusted using internal IMF records.
Third party data.
